Rashi on Shabbat 4a:10:1.hebrew: מעל גבי מקום ד' - דהוי חשוב למיהוי הנחתו הנחה ועקירתו עקירה, וידו לאו מקום ד' הוא. וקתני לה מתני' בין לעקירה בין להנחה, דקתני ונתן לתוך ידו של בעל הבית הרי הנחה, או שנטל מתוכה הרי עקירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 4a:10:1.english: From upon an area of four - For it is [sufficiently] significant for placing [upon it] to be [considered] a placing and lifting [from it] to be [considered] a lifting, and his hand is not an area of four [handbreadths]. And [yet] the Mishnah taught it both with regard to lifting and with regard to placing, as it teaches: "and placed [it] into the hand of the homeowner" — this is placing; "or took [it] from within it" — this is lifting.

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:12:1.hebrew: קלוטה - החפץ, הואיל ונקלט באוירה של רשות הרבים, כמי שהונחה בתוכו הוא, ואע"ג דלא נח:
Rashi on Shabbat 4a:12:1.english: Caught - The object, since it was caught in the airspace of the public domain, is considered as though it was placed within it, even though it did not come to rest.

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:2:1.hebrew: לכי תיכול עלה כורא דמילחא - בבדיחותא אהדר ליה: כשתמדוד לי כור של מלח, אומר לך טעמו של דבר. לישנא אחרינא: לכשתאכל עליה כור של מלח, לא תוכל להשוותם זו לזו:
Rashi on Shabbat 4a:2:1.english: When you eat a kor of salt over it - He answered him in jest: When you measure out a kor of salt for me, I will tell you the reason for the matter. Another explanation: [Even] when you eat a kor of salt over it, you will not be able to equate them to one another.

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:2:2.hebrew: מחשבתו - שנתכוון לפנותה מחצר זה, לא נתקיימה, הלכך לא גזרו. אבל לחצר אחרת, נתקיימה מחשבתו, וגזור, דילמא זימנא אחריתי שדי להו לרה"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 4a:2:2.english: His intention - [In that] he intended to clear it out of this courtyard, [it] was not realized; therefore, they did not decree. But [taking it] to another courtyard, his intention was realized, and they decreed, lest another time he throw them into the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:4:1.hebrew: ולא אידכר - קודם אפייה על שגגתו, שהיא שבת או שמלאכה זו אסורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 4a:4:1.english: And he did not remember - Prior to baking, about his error: that it is Shabbat or that this labor is forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:4:2.english: To whom did they permit [it] - For it does not occur to him to come and ask about this.

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:5:1.english: And rather, that he subsequently remembered - Before the baking.

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:5:2.english: Is he liable - [To bring a] sin-offering upon its baking?

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:5:3.hebrew: תחלתה וסופה - תחלת המלאכה וסופה, לא נודעה לו שגגתו עד שנגמרה עבירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 4a:5:3.english: Its beginning and its end - [At] the beginning of the labor and its end, his error was not known to him until the transgression was completed.

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:7:1.english: To others - Another [person] who saw [it] and came before us to ask [whether he may] remove it before his fellow comes to incur liability for a sin-offering.

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:8:1.hebrew: וכי אומרים לו לאדם - צא וחטא איסור קל, כדי שלא יתחייב חבירך עונש חמור:
Rashi on Shabbat 4a:8:1.english: And do we say to a person - "Go out and sin [by violating] a minor prohibition, so that your fellow will not incur a severe punishment"?

Rashi on Shabbat 4a:9:1.hebrew: בהדיא - סקילה, ובלשון פשיטותא ולא בלשון בעיא, מתני רב אחא בריה דרבא מילתא דרב ביבי:
Rashi on Shabbat 4a:9:1.english: Explicitly - [With the word] "stoning," and in the language of a resolution and not in the language of an inquiry, Rav Aha son of Rava taught Rav Bibi's statement.

Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:10:1.hebrew: והא בעינן עקירה והנחה מעל מקום ד' - אומר ר"ת, דאין רגילות להניח החפץ בפחות מד', וכן היה מסתמא במשכן. ועוד אומר ר"י, ד"אל יצא איש ממקומו" משמע דקאי נמי אחפץ, כלומר ממקומו של חפץ, דרשינן בעירובין (פ"א ד' יז:) ד"אל יצא" – "אל יוציא". אע"ג דפשטיה דקרא קאי אמקומו של אדם, דהיינו ד' אמות, מ"מ משמע נמי מקום החפץ, ואין מקום חשוב בפחות מד':
Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:10:1.english: And don't we require lifting and placing from upon an area of four? - Rabbeinu Tam says that people are not accustomed to place an object in [an area of] less than four [handbreadths], and so it presumably was in the Mishkan (Tabernacle). And furthermore, the Ri says that "let no man go out of his place" implies that it also refers to an object — that is to say, from the place of the object — as we expound in Eruvin (chapter 1, 17b) that "let [no man] go out" [al yetzei] means "do not take out" [al yotzei]. Even though the plain meaning of the verse refers to the place of a person, which is four cubits (amot), nevertheless it also implies the place of the object, and a place is not considered significant if it is less than four [handbreadths].

Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:1:1.hebrew: כאן לחצר אחרת - ואסור להחזירה דקתני, לא להחזירה אצלו קאמר, אלא להחזירה לחצר אחרת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:1:1.english: Here, to a different courtyard - And as for that which it teaches, "it is prohibited to bring it back" — it does not mean bringing it back to himself [i.e., to his own courtyard], but rather bringing it into a different courtyard.

Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:2:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא - בזו כנגד זו איירי, דבדיוטא אחת שנא ושנא, דאיכא איסור חיוב חטאת, דמושיט מרה"י לרה"י דרך רה"ר. א"נ, בדיוטא אחת, וכגון שאין מפסיק שם רה"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:2:1.english: And what is the difference? - [The Gemara] is dealing with [courtyards that are situated] opposite each other [across the public domain], for [if they were] on the same level (bidiota achat) [along the street], there is a vast difference, as there is a prohibition entailing liability for a sin-offering (chatat) for passing [an object] (moshit) from a private domain (reshut hayachid) to a private domain via the public domain (reshut harabbim). Alternatively, [it is dealing with courtyards that are] on the same level, but [in a case] such as where no public domain intervenes there.

Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:5:1.hebrew: ואלא דאהדר ואידכר מי מחייב - תימה, דלישני: אימא לידי (חיוב) איסור חטאת, כדקאמר בסמוך: קודם שיבא לידי איסור סקילה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:5:1.english: And rather, where he then remembered, is he liable? - It is puzzling, for let [the Gemara] answer: "Say: [before he comes] to the prohibition of a sin-offering (issur chattat)" [rather than "liability" (chiyyuv)], just as it says nearby: "before he comes to the prohibition of stoning."

Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:8:1.hebrew: וכי אומרים לו לאדם חטא בשביל שיזכה חבירך - והא דאמר בבכל מערבין (עירובי ן לב: ושם): רבי סבר ניחא ליה לחבר דליעבד איסורא קלילא, ולא ליעבד עם הארץ איסורא רבה - התם כדי שלא יאכל ע"ה טבל על ידו, דאמר לי': "מלא לך כלכלה של תאנים מתאנתי". אבל הכא, שלא נעשה האיסור על ידו, אין אומרים לו: "חטא", אפי' איסור קל, שלא יבא חבירו לידי איסור חמור. ואומר ריב"א, דאפי' למדביק עצמו אין לפשוט משם להתיר, דהתם עדיין לא נעשה האיסור, ומוטב שיעשה איסור קל ולא יעשה איסור חמור על ידו. אבל הכא, המעשה של איסור כבר נעשה, וממילא יגמור - לא יעשה אפי' איסור קל בידים. והא דתנן בהשולח (גיטין דף מא: ושם): מי שחציו עבד וחציו בן חורין, כופין את רבו ועושה אותו בן חורין, ואע"ג דבהאי פירקא (דף לח:) א"ר יהודה: כל המשחרר עבדו עובר בעשה, ד"לעולם בהם תעבודו" - שאני פריה ורביה, דמצוה רבה היא, כדמשני התם בר"א שנכנס לבה"מ ולא מצא שם י', ושחרר את עבדו להשלימו לי': מצוה דרבים שאני. ועוד י"ל, דדוקא היכא דפשע קאמר: "וכי אומרים לו לאדם חטא כדי כו'". ואתי שפיר הא דאמרי' בריש תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף נט. ושם), דאתי עשה דפסח שיש בו כרת ודחי עשה דהשלמה, וקא עברי כהנים בעשה דהשלמה ומקריבין למחוסר כפורים כפרתו כדי שיביא פסחו. וכן בפרק בתרא דעירובין (דף קג: ושם): כהן שנמצא בו יבלת, חבירו חותכה לו לו בשיניו, אע"ג דהוי שבות. וגבי חציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין שנהגו בה מנהג הפקר, וכפו את רבה בהשולח (גיטין דף לח:) - משום שהיתה מחזרת וממציאה עצמה לזנות, ודומי' לאנוסין, והוי נמי כמצוה דרבים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:8:1.english: Do we say to a person: Sin so that your fellow may benefit? - And as for that which is said in [the chapter] "Be-Khol Me'arvin" (Eruvin 32b and elsewhere), [that] Rebbe holds it is preferable for a scrupulous person (chaver) to commit a minor prohibition so that an unlearned person (am ha'aretz) should not commit a major prohibition — there, [it is permitted] in order that the am ha'aretz should not eat untithed produce (tevel) through him, as he said to him: "Fill yourself a basket of figs from my fig tree." But here, where the prohibition was not caused through him, we do not say to him: "Sin," even [by committing] a minor prohibition, so that his fellow will not come to [commit] a severe prohibition. And the Riba says that even regarding the one who stuck [the loaf into the oven] himself, one cannot resolve [the question] from there to permit [it]. For there, the prohibition has not yet been committed, and it is better that he commit a minor prohibition and that a severe prohibition not be committed through him. But here, the act of prohibition has already been done, and it will finish on its own — he should not commit even a minor prohibition actively [with his hands]. And as for that which we learned in the mishna in [the chapter] "Ha-Sholei'ach" (Gittin 41b and elsewhere): "One who is half slave and half free man — they compel his master and he makes him a free man," even though in that same chapter (38b) Rav Yehudah said: "Anyone who frees his slave transgresses a positive commandment, as it is said: 'Forever you shall work them' (Leviticus 25:46)" — procreation (periyah u-reviyah) is different, as it is a great mitzvah, just as it answers there regarding Rabbi Eliezer, who entered the study hall (beit ha-midrash) and did not find ten [men] there, and he freed his slave to complete [the quorum] to ten: a communal mitzvah (mitzvah de-rabbim) is different. And furthermore, it can be said that specifically where [the sinner] was negligent did it say: "Do we say to a person: 'Sin so that [your fellow may benefit]'," etc. And this resolves well that which we say at the beginning of "Tamid Nishchat" (Pesachim 59a and elsewhere), that the positive commandment of the Pesach offering — which carries [the penalty of] excision (karet) — comes and overrides the positive commandment of completion (hashlamah), and the priests transgress the positive commandment of completion and sacrifice the atonement offering for one who lacks atonement (mechusar kippurim) so that he may bring his Pesach offering. And similarly in the last chapter of Eruvin (103b and elsewhere): [in the case of] a priest upon whom a wart was found, his fellow [priest] cuts it off for him with his teeth, even though it is a rabbinic prohibition (shevut). And regarding the maidservant who was half slave and half free woman, with whom they acted licentiously, and they compelled her master [to free her] in "Ha-Sholei'ach" (Gittin 38b) — [that was] because she would pursue [men] and make herself available for prostitution, and [those who sinned with her] were similar to coerced ones, and it is also considered like a communal mitzvah.

Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:9:1.hebrew: קודם שיבא לידי איסור סקילה - וא"ת: מאי בעיא היא זו אם התירו לרדותה? פשיטא שלא ישמע לנו אם נאסור לו! ותי' ריב"א, דאם לא התירו לא מיחייב סקילה, כיון שמניח מלרדות ע"י מה שאנו אוסרין לו. וכן בפסחים בס"פ האשה (דף צב. ושם): ערל, הזאה ואיזמל העמידו דבריהם במקום כרת, אלמא לא מיחייב כרת, הואיל ורבנן הוא דאסרי ליה למיעבד פסח. וא"ת: והיכי אתי לידי חיוב סקילה? והא התראת ספק הוא, דבשעה שהדביק פת בתנור, שמא היה בדעתו לרדותה קודם שיבא לידי איסור סקילה, ומה שלא רדה - שמא שכח ההתראה? ותי' ריב"א, דכיון שהדביק תוך כדי דבור של התראה, ובודאי תאפה אם לא ירדנה - לאו התראת ספק הוא, דודאי לא היה בדעתו לרדות קודם אפייה. ולא הוי התראת ספק אלא בלוקח אם על הבנים, למ"ד בפ' ואלו הן הלוקין (מכות דף טו.) בטלו ולא בטלו, דשמא לא ישבור כנפיה או לא ישחטנה, ועכשיו שמשבר כנפיה אין יכולין להתרותו, דלא הויא התראה אלא על הלאו, והלאו כבר עבר. וכן בשבועה: "שלא אוכל ככר זו אם אוכל זו", ואכליה לאיסוריה והדר אכליה לתנאיה, דכשמתרין בו בשעת אכילת איסור, עדיין מחוסר מעשה אכילה של תנאי קודם שיתחייב מלקות. אבל הכא, כשמדביק פת בתנור, אין האפייה מחוסרת מעשה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:9:1.english: Before he comes to the prohibition of stoning - And if you will say: What inquiry is this [regarding] whether they permitted him to scrape it out? It is obvious that he will not listen to us if we forbid him [to do so]! And Riba answered that if they did not permit [him], he is not liable to stoning, since he refrains from scraping [the bread] out on account of what we forbid him. And similarly in Pesachim at the end of the chapter "Ha-Ishah" (92a and there): [in the cases of] an uncircumcised person (arel), sprinkling [purification water] (haza'ah), and a circumcision scalpel (izmel), [the Sages] upheld their words in a situation [leading to passive omission] of karet. Evidently, he is not liable to karet, since it is the Rabbis who forbade him to perform the Pesach offering. And if you will say: But how could he come to liability for stoning? For isn't this an uncertain forewarning (hatra'at safek) - as at the time he attached the bread to the oven, perhaps it was his intention to scrape it out before it would come to the prohibition of stoning, and as for the fact that he did not scrape it out, perhaps he forgot the forewarning? And Riba answered that since he attached [the bread] within the time needed for a spoken phrase (toch kedei dibbur) of the forewarning, and it will certainly bake if he does not scrape it out, it is not an uncertain forewarning, for he certainly did not intend to scrape it out prior to baking. And it is only considered an uncertain forewarning in [a case such as] one who takes the mother [bird] upon the young, according to the one who holds in the chapter "Ve-Elu Hen Ha-Lokin" (Makkot 15a) [that the dispute is whether he is liable once] he nullified it [the positive commandment] or did not nullify it - for perhaps he will not break its wings or will not slaughter it [and will instead send it away]; and now, when he breaks its wings, they cannot forewarn him, because forewarning can only be given for [the violation of] the negative commandment, and the negative commandment has already passed. And similarly in [the case of] an oath: "[I swear] that I will not eat this loaf if I eat that [other] one," and he ate the forbidden [loaf] and then ate the conditional [loaf] - for when they forewarn him at the time he eats the forbidden [loaf], [his liability] is still lacking the act of eating the conditional [loaf] before he becomes liable for lashes. But here, when he attaches bread to the oven, the baking is not lacking any action.

Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:9:2.hebrew: מתני לה בהדיא - אית ספרים דגרסי בעי רב ביבי, ומתני בהדיא בבעיא דרב ביבי איסור סקילה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4a:9:2.english: Teaches it explicitly - There are texts that read "Rav Bibi inquired" [ba'ei Rav Bibi, rather than "Rav Bibi said"], and [according to this version, Rav Acha] teaches explicitly in Rav Bibi's inquiry: "a prohibition punishable by stoning" [issur sekilah].
